records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The public embed script silently requires `discourseUrl` to end in `/`, so a normal origin URL produces an invalid `https://hostembed/best` endpoint.
records.rationale: The new embed.js line `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` blindly string-concatenates; there is no check or normalization ensuring `discourseUrl` ends in '/'. If the embedder supplies e.g. 'https://forum.example.com' the resulting URL becomes 'https://forum.example.comembed/best', breaking the embed. The defect mechanism is fully verifiable from the diff itself.
records.stripped_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The public embed script silently requires `discourseUrl` to end in `/`, so a normal origin URL produces an invalid `https://hostembed/best` endpoint.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every cache miss enqueues before validating embed_url, so forged requests with unique invalid URLs can grow the job queue without bound.
records.rationale: In embed_controller.rb#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns nil, the controller unconditionally does Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) with only the user-supplied embed_url (validated only as non-nil via params.require). URL/host validation happens later in TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, and the throttle (retrieved_recently?) is keyed per embed_url ('retrieved:#{@embed_url}' with 60s expiry), so each unique forged URL bypasses the rate limit and enqueues a new job. records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — Disabling retries means any transient feed failure or malformed item aborts the run and leaves all remaining updates stale until the next hourly poll.
records.rationale: The finding is factually true (`sidekiq_options retry: false` is in poll_feed.rb) but the stated consequence is self-limiting and intentional: the job is scheduled with `recurrence { hourly }`, so the 'stale until the next hourly poll' outcome is at most a one-hour delay, which is the natural cadence of a scheduled poller anyway. Disabling retries on a scheduled job is a deliberate design choice, not a defect or substantive review concern; this is a preference-level observation without decision-relevant material consequence.

records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:134 — RSS and readability imports are stored as raw HTML without sanitization, allowing feed or page content to persist executable markup and trigger stored XSS for forum readers.
records.rationale: The diff adds Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] where cook() returns raw unfiltered, and TopicEmbed.import passes RSS/readability-fetched content as raw_html via PostCreator with skip_validations. Readability's tags/attributes options only select content, not sanitize; feed content (CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)) is stored as executable markup. Nothing in the diff sanitizes scripts/event handlers, so stored XSS for readers is a real mechanism introduced here.
records.stripped_text: app/models/post.rb:134 — RSS and readability imports are stored as raw HTML without sanitization, allowing feed or page content to persist executable markup and trigger stored XSS for forum readers.

records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported feed HTML is stored as raw_html without sanitization, allowing a compromised feed to persist executable markup in every rendered topic/embed.
records.rationale: Diff confirms the mechanism: TopicEmbed.import passes feed contents as raw with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], and Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for that method; Jobs::PollFeed imports `i.content` with only CGI.unescapeHTML (no sanitization, unlike import_remote's readability tag whitelist), and the content is then rendered unsanitized via `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb. A malicious feed can persist executable markup.
records.stripped_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Imported feed HTML is stored as raw_html without sanitization, allowing a compromised feed to persist executable markup in every rendered topic/embed.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Defaulting every existing post to cook_method 1 marks legacy posts as raw HTML, bypassing the normal cooking and sanitization pipeline on subsequent cooks.
records.rationale: The migration defaults cook_method to 1, and Post.cook_methods defines Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), where the first symbol :regular corresponds to value 1 (Discourse Enum is 1-indexed). So the migration sets existing posts to :regular, not raw HTML — the diff contradicts the finding's claim that defaulting to 1 marks legacy posts as raw HTML.
